description:
## Problem

Reach uses :erlang.apply/3 in its HEEx parser to dynamically invoke parser modules. Module.concat is used extensively for creating module names from AST parts. Both are dynamic code execution vectors.

## Evidence

From reach:
- reach/lib/reach/plugins/live_view/heex/parser.ex:46: :erlang.apply(@parser, :parse, [source, parser_opts])
- reach/lib/reach/frontend/elixir.ex: Module.concat(parts) for dynamic module resolution
- reach/lib/reach/macro_fact.ex: Module.concat(parts) for macro analysis

## Expected Behavior

- :erlang.apply should be flagged as dynamic code execution
- Module.concat with non-literal args should be flagged as atom table exhaustion risk

## Suggested Fix

Add to rules/elixir-sinks.kdl Elixir-Code-Execution:
- sink ":erlang.apply" arg=0 { fix "Avoid dynamic function application with untrusted input" }
- sink "Module.concat" arg=0 { sanitizer "Module.safe_concat?" }

Note: Module.concat with atom-only args is safe. Only flag when args come from string conversion.
title: Elixir: add :erlang.apply and Module.concat as dynamic code execution sinks
